reasons: CS4261 requires MA1100/MA1100T/CS1231S/CS1231 and MA2001/MA1101R/MA1311/MA1508E/MA1513/MA1522. The student has CS1231S but lacks any of the required linear algebra/calculus prerequisites (MA1100, MA1508E, MA1513, MA1522, etc.) to satisfy the MA component for CS4261 in Semester 5.

CS2109S requires (YSC2229 or CS2040S/C/HS/DE) and (MA1511+MA1512 or MA1521 or MA2002 or MA1102R or MA1312 or MA1507 or MA1505). The student has MA1521, satisfying the math part. However, they lack CS2040S/C/HS/DE or YSC2229. CS2040S requires CS1231/CS1231S/MA1100/MA1100T. The student has CS1231S, so they can take CS2040S. But CS2040S is a prerequisite for CS2109S. CS2109S must come before CS3230. CS3230 requires CS2040S/C/HS/DE/MA1100/MA1100T/CS1231S/CS1231. The student has CS1231S, so they can take CS3230 directly? No, CS3230 prerequisite is (YSC2229 or CS2040S or CS2040 or CS2040C or CS2040DE or CS2040HS) AND (CS1231 or CS1231S or MA1100T or MA1100). The student has CS1231S, so the second part is met. But the first part requires CS2040S/C/HS/DE/MA1100/MA1100T. The student does NOT have MA1100 or MA1100T. They have CS1231S. So they MUST take CS2040S (or C/HS/DE) before CS3230. CS2040S requires CS1231S (met) and CS1010... (met via CS1101S). So CS2040S is possible. Then CS2109S requires CS2040S. So CS2040S -> CS2109S -> CS3230 chain exists. However, the fatal flaw is CS4261's MA prerequisite.
